Hi to everybody (and merry X-mas)

Tournaments are tournaments (some people go to win only), but, during
friendly play, what's the deck type you hate most ?
I sometimes (lot of times) play with a intercept wall, and my friends
simply throw anithing to me when we set plaiyng seats and they discover
to be my predators.
By my side I hate wheenie/Anarch Revolt/Delayng Tactics decks 'couse
they shorten the games (and are so difficult to stop without 15+ Sudden
Reversal).
Generally speaking I hate decks that rely on a table reaction to deal
with; I mean, Toreador with 3+ Aching Beauty on them are nightmares to
stop just becouse there are (usually) not enough Sudden Reversals
available, and cross table players are unwilling to "waste" theyr to
stop a ally....the same for the wheenie above or for vote wheenies that
can be stopped only by a four players coaliction ready to vote against
them.
Generally speaking, I like slow games, where strategies other than pure
speed may develop freely...and play skill can match pure deckbuilding
skill (maybe becouse I'm poor at this last one).

We discussed about the best 5 vamps, the whorst cards, the stupid-est
(?) special ability...end this 2000 with a all-around discussion forum.

Thank you
akaisuisei

http://www.deja.com/

Messages.Author: Ian Lee
Messages.Body:
>during
>friendly play, what's the deck type you hate most ?

This question, by itself, was a revelation. In thinking over an answer, what
kept popping up was one trick pony decks - decks that did one thing over and
over again. It doesn't matter whether it is stealth bleed, Tradition Tap, rush
Grapple, KRR(eally)Contested, or whatever. The revelation part is that these
(one trick pony decks, though usually with bad cards or bad combos) are the
sorts of experimental/concept decks I build just to have more decks on hand. I
suppose it's time to build decks that do more things.

Of course, it's also boring to play against more interesting decks if you play
against them often enough. And, it can be painful to get a bad match up,
though that's hardly under anyone's control.

akais...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Tournaments are tournaments (some people go to win only), but,
> during friendly play, what's the deck type you hate most?

I'd have to say my least favorite deck to be on the business end of is a
poorly built Ravnos "Lock Down" deck. Y'know the type...Pentex
Subversion/Brainwash/Sensory Deprivation.

When I say "poorly built," I mean that's all it does...it keeps the
prey's vampires from doing anything. What it doesn't do is bleed for
much, meaning the prey sits there twiddling his thumbs waiting for the
Ravnos deck's predator to oust him.

A well built "Lock Down" deck will capitalize on the weakness it
has created by bleeding for 2 or 3 per minion fairly regularly. Which of
course, results in a quicker VP for the Ravnos deck.

Outside of that, I'd have to say non-innovative S&B decks and vote
decks. They're fine if they do something unusual.

OTOH, Rush combat decks tend to be pretty popular in my area, so it's
not uncommon to see some pretty impressive battles between vampires. Any
true fan of VTES loves to see a good fight.

Regards,

Interesting point. I do have to say that there isn't a single deck that
annoys me. Though there are playstyles that do, I'll get back to that
later.
All is fair love and JYHAD IMO. Of course there should be a kind of
friendliness in friendly games, still the object of the game it to
gather VP's, no matter what kind of environment. The only thing that it
good about frienly games, is that you get your ass kicked, without it
having repercussions unlike a tournament. Sure peope can play cheesy,
degenerate, good and evil decks, but that is part of the game, and no
deck is the end of it all. If it were, we'd all have stopped playing 2-3
years ago. And yes sometimes some player plays a hidiously effective
deck, so what? Next game I'll modify my deck, or play another, and we'll
see whether it is so good. That is the charm of the game IMO.
There are however playstyles which I really hate.
The "I-want-to-be-the-last-at-the-table" strategy, generally intercept
decks without forward motion. The "I'll-keep-everyone-in-the-game"
strategy. Even worse is the "I-need-kill-my-predator-first" srategy, and
i can think of several others. Basically I dislike any strategy, player,
that does not try to maximize his/her efforts to oust a prey. I have
been prey to numerous -I sit and do nothing-decks/players, and swept
tables. But having him as grand-predator will end your game before it
started. Which leaves you with no fun at all. Which is a big part of the
game for me. Biggest problem is the balance between competativeness and
fun. While I can get my kicks from a *very* competative game, others
cannot. This is reflected in the respective decks.
But to come back to the question of hated decks, i think that these
degenerate hated decks *should* be played, if only to make the metagame
evolve/change, and explore the vast depths of this game.

Just my babbling,

the Animalism bleed untap, and you are good to go against everything
but Ridiculous Stealth Bleed (add Deflections) or Ridiculously Insane
Combat (add Skin of Steel, they have Fortitude). Some of this depends
on your metagame. =)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Noal McDonald <dhar...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> Y'know...people tend to want to block Gangrels with Tier of
> Souls and J.S.Simmons when they bleed with Force of Will. The whole
> bleed for 5 thing gets their attention.
>
> But that begs the question, if Force of Will gets blocked, can you use
> Form of Mist to restart the action or do you go to torpor right away?

Form of Mist (superior) continues the action - it doesn't restart
the action.

The damage from Force of Will occurs after the action is resolved,
so Form of Mist can safely continue it. The "or combat" bit on
Force of Will is just redundant with the "after the action" bit.

i agree. But I also strongly dislike using social pressure of the
form "you can't play that deck anymore, it's no fun". I prefer to
simply adjust the metagame to deal with it until the deck goes away.

if you notice, both those decks aren't designed specifically to
-counter- his strategy, they're designed to ignore it. A big DOM deck
can do all KINDS of things besides just Govern backwards and gain
pool; the idea is simply to use the Govern backwards concept to gain
pool outside of your master phase. Same with a Bewitching/Cons.
Boon/Voter Cap deck; it can do lots of things besides that, but it
just uses a form of pool gain that isn't in your Master phase.

It becomes a local playgroup metagame; especially if you have someone
who likes to play the same deck over and over. We discovered that
long ago in our group; if you brought the same deck too many times,
someone would "accidentally" have something that contained the counter
to that deck. If you had a monster Gangrel Fortitude
prevent-and-bleed deck, you could expect that the Tremere with
Guardian Angels would show up to the table eventually, shifting the
game around. If Potence IG was the order of the day, obf/cel gun
decks or Obedience would start to show up. If weenies come around too
much, Atonement starts to make an appearance. (And Todd discovered
that Drawing out the Beast fries the Assamites pretty good.)

After awhile of this ever-shifting metagame, people began to rarely if
ever play the same deck two weeks in a row, and never twice in one
night. The game around here has slowly shifted to what the designers
intended; you never DO know what your opponents have, so you will need
to be prepared for everything. Sure, when I build a deck I keep it
built for a month or so, and play it on a few occasions to test it out
and tweak it some; and if it's especially fun I keep it built and
bring it out every so often. But if I tried to play my flung-junk
bleed deck every week, I would quickly find either an awful lot of
Drawing out the Beast hitting the table, or a lot of pesky Ivory
Bow/Flamethrower decks, or a lot of Celerity gun decks.

As it stands now, you have NO idea what you'll run into when you come
to our table; last night's first game looked like this (prey
downwards):

Me: AUS/obf intercept with Disguised .44s (swept)
Pat: Shadow Twin/Fame with Embraces, Humanitas, and Catacombs
Tatu: a Rob Treasure style (Tatu's words) toolbox voter/bloater
Mike: this vote deck was brought to you by the letter "A"
(alexandra, arika, anson)

Not exactly your run of the mill setup. Someone bringing a "stock"
deck into this environment is likely to have a rude surprise, too;
especially if they sit down in the wrong place.

[The deck you described above would've gone absolutely nowhere, by the
way; I'd have intercepted and killed all the weenies, Pat would've
Shadow Twinned them all into torpor and yo-yoed the Famous one, Mike
would've bounced the bleeds, bloated like a pig, and voted down the
Anarchs if he gave a damn (two Master actions means one Sudden
Reversal doesn't cut it anymore), and Tatu's deck would probably have
done the same since he was using a lot of 4th Tradition.]

Sometimes it's necessary to specifically avoid a deck. But a lot of
times, just building something that's reasonably functional on its own
will do the trick.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <92crlm$7te$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>, bobby_doc
<bobb...@my-deja.com> writes

>a friend of mine played a weenie presence with 10% Sudden Reversal,
>to stop Blood Dolls and Minion Taps.
>Also packs Anarch Revolt and some Parthenon.
>Of course bleed cards and S:CE.

A combat deck should be taking out its minions very quickly. Immortal
Grapple, Dog Pack, Telepathic Tracking, Thoughts Betrayed and so forth
are all potential cards to get around S:CE.

A vote deck can now have weenie defence in the form of Rabble Rouse (or
whatever it's called, I don't have the new card lists yet). It can also
Ancilla Empowerment, and get blood back with Voter Captivation,
Tithings, Ancient Influence (which also hurts the weenie deck), Transfer
of Power, Consanguineous Boon, Political Stranglehold and the like.
throwing Kine Resources at the weenie deck, if necessary. It can
Dramatic Upheaval/Kindred Restructure out of the way, along with getting
rid of the Anarch Revolt or Disputing the Parthenon.

A !Malk bleed deck can always back bleed to force the Presence deck off
the table.

A deck with AUS or dom/DOM can bounce the bleeds, and you often don't
need to bounce that many to seriously bugger up both your predator (the
presence deck) or your prey.

The presence deck will either need some stealth (which is more difficult
in a weenie pre deck), or taps. With minor intercept, you're likely to
be able to do well. 2nd Tradition, Forced Awakening, Wake with
Evening's Freshness, Eternal Vigilance, Metro Underground, Guardian
Angel and Atonement are all candidates for defence against weenie
hordes. If you're playing Tremere, you have Justine - but you have
bigger problems to worry about if you're playing Tremere, like having a
good deck to play. ;)
